rows.grounds: compound of agniṣṭoma (a Vedic soma sacrifice) and phala (fruit, result); accusative object of the implied attainment
refers to the worshipper of Jalpīśa mentioned in the preceding verse
future result of the prescribed worship
possessive qualifier of the vocative addressee
vocative address to the interlocutor in the revelatory dialogue

items.question: What sacrificial merit does the prescribed worship of Jalpīśa confer upon the devotee?
premises: The preceding verses prescribe worship of Jalpīśa, the great liṅga.
The speaker addresses a beloved interlocutor in a revelatory dialogue.
The stated outcome of that worship is the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
items.inference: Therefore, the devotee who worships Jalpīśa obtains the merit equivalent to performing an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
uncertainties: The specific identity of the beloved addressee is not stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: O my beloved, he will obtain the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
